species.harvesting_etiquette: Take small clusters of leaves or fallen twigs (datun). Never strip trunk bark.
Trifoliate leaves (belpatra) are sacred. Pluck whole 3-leaf clusters gently; do not tear twigs.
Tradition advises plucking leaves only after bathing, gently pinching tops to encourage bushier growth. Do not uproot.
Leaves exchanged during Dussehra. Pluck only a few leaflets; respect the tree as state tree of Rajasthan.
Revered across Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions. Collect naturally fallen leaves or take 1-2 green leaves gently.
National tree of India. For Vat Savitri puja, perform circumambulation; never lop aerial prop roots.
Essential for Lord Ganesha worship in bunches of 21 knots (3-bladed nodes). Cut tender green tips gently.

species.toxicity_details: HIGHLY TOXIC! All parts contain tropane alkaloids (scopolamine, atropine). Deadly if ingested. Wash hands thoroughly after handling.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Wear gloves or pluck strictly by the stem without bruising fruit thorns. Keep out of reach of children and pets.

species.toxicity_details: TOXIC SAP! Milky latex causes severe corneal damage and irritation on eye contact. Ingestion causes vomiting and cardiotoxicity.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Garlands of Aak flowers are offered to Lord Shiva and Hanuman. Never touch eyes after plucking; wash hands with soap.

species.toxicity_details: LETHALLY TOXIC! Contains oleandrin and cardiac glycosides. Ingesting even a single leaf or petal can cause fatal arrhythmias.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Red and yellow flowers offered in Shiva pujas. Wash hands after plucking. Never ingest.
Leaves (Amra pallava) used for Toran and Kalash. Pluck only 5-leaf or 7-leaf clusters cleanly; do not break fruiting spurs.
Red flowers sacred to Goddess Kali, Durga, and Ganesha. Pluck fresh fully bloomed flowers by the pedicel.
Sacred during Amla Navami and Kartika. Collect ripe fruit gently without snapping delicate fruiting branchlets.
Strip fresh pinnate leaves gently for cooking. Leave main branches intact.
Pinch whole sprigs near the top to encourage bushy regrowth. Do not strip single leaves from lower stem.

species.toxicity_details: Traditional respiratory remedy. Not medical advice.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Take mature healthy leaves; avoid uprooting wild shrubs.

species.toxicity_details: Ayurvedic Rasayana. Consult practitioner before consuming.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Giloy climbing on Neem is traditionally prized ("Neem Giloy"). Cut finger-thick stem pieces only; leave root attachment intact so vine survives.
STRICT PROTECTION: Protected under national forestry laws. Harvesting wood or injuring wild trees is an offense. Coordinates are fuzzed for conservation.
ENDANGERED SPECIES: Endemic to Seshachalam hills. Strictly protected under Wildlife Protection Act. Coordinates fuzzed.
Unique in Hindu puja tradition: Parijat flowers that have naturally fallen on a clean cloth are accepted for worship. Do not pluck buds forcefully.
True Sita Ashoka is increasingly rare (often confused with Polyalthia longifolia / False Ashoka). Do not peel wild bark; admire and conserve.
Harvest fallen ripe purple fruit or shake lower branches gently into a cloth. Never hack high limbs.
Revered cardioprotective bark. In wild trees, never ring-bark or peel completely around circumference. Take only small longitudinal strips.
Primary ingredient of Triphala ("Mother of Herbs"). Collect ripe fallen fruit from ground.
Triphala component. Collect mature fallen nuts.
Roots are harvested only from mature cultivated plants after berries turn red. Leave wild plants undisturbed.
Fiery orange flowers traditionally used to make non-toxic natural Holi colors (Tesu) and offered in Shiva/Saraswati pujas. Leaves stitched into eco-friendly dining plates (Pattal).

species.toxicity_details: Seeds have purgative action; use fruit pulp strictly under guidance.
species.harvesting_etiquette: State flower of Kerala (Kani Konna), essential for Vishu festival ritual arrangement. Pluck hanging flower racemes carefully.
Revered in Krishna lore (Vrindavan). Fragrant ball-shaped orange flowers bloom with monsoon onset. Harvest naturally fallen blossoms.
Tiny star-shaped cream flowers retain sweet aroma even after drying. Gather fallen flowers from ground for puja.
Pluck ripe pods when shells turn brittle and brown. Tender sour leaves used in South Indian cooking.
Deep royal blue flowers are sacred to Lord Shiva and Goddess Durga. Pluck individual blossoms by stem.

species.toxicity_details: Medhya Rasayana for cognitive support. Not medical advice.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Grows in wet, marshy soil and pond edges. Cut top creeping shoots; leave root nodes in mud so colony regenerates.
King of hair rejuvenation herbs (Keshya). White daisy-like flowers. Pluck aerial shoots with scissors.

species.toxicity_details: Yellow aloin sap at leaf base can cause laxative cramping; drain before using inner gel.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Slice lowest, fattest outer leaf cleanly with knife close to stem. Never pull or tear center leaves.
Twigs traditionally used in sacred rituals; rinds used for digestion remedies. Pick ripe fruits with scissors.
Tender leaf shoots used for toothache and oral rinses. Pick fruit when pale greenish-yellow.
Cut lower leaf stalks 2 inches above ground; clumps thrive with regular trimming for herbal tea.

species.toxicity_details: DEADLY TOXIN: Raw seeds contain ricin, one of the most potent plant toxins known. Ingestion of 2-4 seeds can be fatal. External oil is safe.
species.harvesting_etiquette: WARNED: Never allow children to play with spiny seed pods. Large peltate leaves used externally for warm compress.
National flower of India; supreme offering to Goddess Lakshmi and Saraswati. Cut flower stems cleanly with aquatic knife without dragging silt.
Ubiquitous for festival garlands and Diwali torans. Snap flower heads at the calyx node.
Harvest swollen white unopened buds in late evening; they unfurl into intensely fragrant blossoms overnight.
Giant leaves used for pristine sacred feast servings and Satyanarayan mandap pillar pillars. Cut single leaf along petiole cleanly.
Largest tree-borne fruit. Harvest with sickle when spines flatten and fruit gives hollow thud.
Tree of Life for tribal and forest communities across central India. Plump sugary cream flowers drop at night; gather at dawn from cleaned forest floor.
Lemons offered as protective garland to Goddess Kali and Mariamman. Clip ripe yellow fruit with clippers to avoid tearing thorn branches.
Paan leaves are sacred in all Hindu rituals (Tambulam). Pluck whole glossy heart-shaped leaves with full petiole intact.
Whole fresh turmeric plant with green leaves offered during Pongal, Makar Sankranti, and Chhath. Rhizome dug when leaves wither.
Fresh plant with green aerial shoots offered in Chhath Daura. Dig out mature knobby rhizome in winter.
Abundant native shade and timber tree. Pluck fallen pods or small twigs.
Spectacular avenue tree blooming in blazing scarlet blossoms during Indian summer heat. Enjoy shade and view.
Giant thorny buttressed trunk. Fleshy flower buds cooked as delicacy in Purvanchal. Collect fallen buds from ground.
Traditional natural toothbrush (Babool datun) promotes gum health. Cut small straight green twigs carefully around thorns.
Creeping fan-shaped leaves in moist shade. Clip leaves along runner; do not uproot crown.
Thorny climbing shrub with feathery cladodes. Dig tubers from cultivated plants only.

species.toxicity_details: Potent reserpine alkaloid lowers blood pressure drastically. Overdose causes extreme hypotension and bradycardia. Fuzzed for conservation.
species.harvesting_etiquette: PROTECTED HERB: Wild harvesting banned under CITES Appendix II. Exact coordinates fuzzed.

species.toxicity_details: King of Bitters. Powerful liver tonic and immune herb. Extremely bitter taste.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Harvest before winter flowering for highest andrographolide potency.
Alpine Himalayan herb. Overexploited in wild. Fuzzed coordinates.
"That which renews the body" (Punarnava). Cut prostrate leafy stems; leave deep taproot intact.
THREATENED: Chemical hacking for resin has caused severe wild decline in Rajasthan and Gujarat. Strictly protected.
Grows between 3000m-5000m in alpine Himalayas. Wild harvest strictly regulated. Fuzzed coordinates.
Famed gynecological and wound-healing herb in Ayurveda. Take small bark flakes only.
Premier blood purifying and natural red dye creeper. Prickly stems climb over bushes.
Prostrate herb with spiny 5-horned fruit resembling cow hoof (Go-kshura). Wear sturdy shoes when collecting.
Golden fragrant stamens offered in sacred pujas. Beautiful pink-red young foliage. Collect flowers cleanly.
"Bala" confers physical strength. Heart-shaped velvety leaves with yellow flowers. Gather aerial parts.
Harvest from coppiced stems only; outer bark scraped away to yield paper-thin quills of sweet inner bark.
Clove buds harvested before turning pink; sun-dried until deep brown. Paired cloves sacred in Havan and Aarti.
King of Spices. Woody vine climbing on living support trees (Areca, Silver Oak). Pick whole berry spikes when one or two berries turn red.
Trikatu ingredient for digestion and respiratory health. Pick firm green spikes before fully turning black.
Prime anti-parasitic and deworming herb in Ayurveda (Krimighna). Gather ripe globular berries.

species.toxicity_details: Potent stimulant laxative; short-term use only. Consult healthcare provider.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Collect mature bluish-green leaflets when plants begin flowering in arid zones.
Harvest spikes in dry early morning before morning wind scatters seeds. Mucilaginous husk aids gut health.
Essential ingredient in Paan and Ayurvedic dental remedies. Never injure main trunk.
Sacred seat of Lord Dattatreya. Cluster figs grow directly on trunk bark. Eat fruit only after checking for symbiotic wasps.
King of Timber. Giant coarse leaves turn reddish when crushed. Do not chop live trees.
Sacred to Goddess Sarna and Lord Buddha (born and attained Mahaparinirvana under Sal trees). Fragrant Ral resin burnt in pujas.
The divine "Kalpavriksha". Whole green or brown coconut with husk placed atop Purna Kalash in every Vedic ceremony.

species.toxicity_details: Seeds contain irritant alkaloids; do not crush or swallow seeds.
species.harvesting_etiquette: Delicious fragrant autumn fruit. Pick when skin gaps turn cream/white between green segments.
Ber fruit sacred in Maha Shivratri offerings and Shabari Bhakti tradition. Harvest golden-yellow ripe fruits gently among spiny twigs.

festivals.description_en: The great night of Lord Shiva. Devotees offer Bilva leaves, Dhatura fruits, and white/blue flowers for the auspicious Lingam Abhishekam.
festivals.description_hi: भगवान शिव का पावन महापर्व। शिवलिंग अभिषेक के लिए बेलपत्र, धतूरा, आक और कनेर के पुष्प विशेष रूप से अर्पित किए जाते हैं।

checklist.purpose: Primary offering to Shiva Lingam; symbolizes the Trinetra (3 eyes)
checklist.notes: Take 3-leaf clusters that are unblemished and clean.

checklist.purpose: Sacred offering to neutralize cosmic poisons (Halahala)
checklist.notes: CAUTION: Toxic! Handle carefully by the stem.

checklist.purpose: Offering of sacred white/purple flowers and garland to Shiva
checklist.notes: Do not touch eyes after handling milky sap.

checklist.purpose: Offering of vibrant fragrant flowers
checklist.notes: Wash hands after plucking.

checklist.purpose: Traditional Shami leaf offering to Lord Shiva
checklist.notes: Pluck a few leaflets gently.

festivals.description_en: Celebration of the victory of righteousness over evil. Exchanging Shami and Apta leaves symbolizes mutual prosperity ("Gold exchange").
festivals.description_hi: बुराई पर अच्छाई की विजय का पर्व। शमी और आप्टा के पत्तों को "सोना" मानकर एक-दूसरे को आदरपूर्वक भेंट करने की परंपरा है।

checklist.purpose: Auspicious Shami leaves for greeting elders and friends as "Son-patta"
checklist.notes: Take only a small sprig.

checklist.purpose: Mango leaves for doorstep Toran to welcome prosperity
checklist.notes: Tie onto thread with marigold flowers.

festivals.description_en: Welcoming Lord Ganesha with the traditional 21-sacred leaf (Eka-vimshati Patrika) and Durva grass rituals.
festivals.description_hi: भगवान गणेश का जन्मोत्सव। 21 प्रकार के पवित्र पत्रों (एकविंशति पत्रिका) और दूर्वा की 21 गांठों से विशेष पूजन किया जाता है।

checklist.purpose: Indispensable 21 Durva grass bunches offered to Ganesha
checklist.notes: Rinse with clean water before offering.

checklist.purpose: Lord Ganesha's most beloved red flower (Rakta Pushpa)
checklist.notes: Offer fresh morning bloomed flowers.

checklist.purpose: Part of the 21 Patrika sacred botanical set
checklist.notes: Sacred element of the 21-leaf ritual.

checklist.purpose: Shami patra for Ganesha Sahasranama puja
checklist.notes: Brings wisdom and barrier removal.

festivals.description_en: Festival of lights. Homes are adorned with entrance Torans crafted from fresh Mango and Ashoka leaves to invite Goddess Lakshmi.
festivals.description_hi: दीपोत्सव एवं माता लक्ष्मी का आगमन पर्व। घर के मुख्य द्वार पर आम और अशोक के पत्तों का तोरण बांधना अत्यंत शुभ माना जाता है।

checklist.purpose: Entrance Toran and Kalash Sthapana for Lakshmi Puja
checklist.notes: Pick healthy unblemished leaves.

checklist.purpose: Tulsi leaves for offering to Lord Vishnu & Dhanvantari
checklist.notes: Do not pluck on Amavasya evening.

festivals.description_en: Ancient solar thanksgiving festival celebrated with profound reverence along riverbanks. Offerings comprise pure, unhybridized agricultural plants.
festivals.description_hi: सूर्यदेव एवं छठी मइया का महापर्व। सूप और दउरा में ईख, अदरक का पौधा, हल्दी का पौधा, केला और बेल फल अर्पित किए जाते हैं।

checklist.purpose: Offering of sacred Bael fruit in the Daura/Arghya
checklist.notes: Unbroken fruit preferred.

checklist.purpose: Dry mango wood for the pristine Havana and sacred stove fire
checklist.notes: Collect only naturally fallen dry wood.

festivals.description_en: Ceremonial marriage of the Holy Basil (Tulsi) with Lord Vishnu (Shaligrama), inaugurating the Hindu wedding season.
festivals.description_hi: तुलसी जी का भगवान शालिग्राम के साथ दिव्य विवाह। इस दिन से मांगलिक कार्यों और विवाह का शुभारंभ होता है।

checklist.purpose: The central deity of the ceremony
checklist.part_needed: Living potted plant adorned as a bride
checklist.notes: Decorate with sugarcane mandap and haldi-kumkum.

checklist.purpose: Amla branch placed in the Tulsi pot representing Vishnu
checklist.part_needed: Tender branch with leaves and gooseberry fruit
checklist.notes: Symbolizes the presence of Lord Damodara.

festivals.description_en: Married women observe fast and pray around the sacred Banyan tree for marital bliss and spouse's longevity, commemorating Savitri's devotion.
festivals.description_hi: सुहागिन महिलाओं द्वारा पति की दीर्घायु और अखंड सौभाग्य हेतु वट (बरगद) वृक्ष की परिक्रमा और सूत बांधने का पावन व्रत।

checklist.purpose: Living Banyan tree for parikrama (circumambulation) and thread wrapping
checklist.notes: Find the nearest living Banyan tree. Do not cut branches.

festivals.description_en: Deccan and Marathi New Year celebration. Neem leaves and flowers are mixed with jaggery to symbolize life's dual experiences of bitter and sweet.
festivals.description_hi: नववर्ष उत्सव। जीवन के सुख-दुख का प्रतीक माने जाने वाले नीम के पत्ते और फूल गुड़ के साथ ग्रहण किए जाते हैं।

checklist.purpose: Essential ingredient for Ugadi Pachadi / Bevu-Bella
checklist.part_needed: Tender fresh leaves and small white flowers
checklist.notes: Pluck morning fresh flowers and tiny young leaf tips.

checklist.purpose: Fresh green mangoes for Pachadi and entrance Toran
checklist.notes: Symbolizes new beginnings.

festivals.description_en: Worship of the 9 sacred plants (Navapatrika / Kola Bou) embodying 9 manifestations of Goddess Durga.
festivals.description_hi: माँ दुर्गा के नौ रूपों का प्रतीक मानी जाने वाली नौ पवित्र वनस्पतियों (नवपत्रिका) का विधिवत आवाहन एवं पूजन।

checklist.purpose: Belpatrika: Invocation of Goddess Shivaa
checklist.notes: One of the nine sacred plants bound together.

checklist.purpose: Ashoka: Invocation of Goddess Shokarahita
checklist.notes: Bound into the Kola Bou bundle.

checklist.purpose: Daily Pushpanjali to Mother Durga
checklist.notes: Goddess Durga's favored floral offering.

festivals.description_en: Harvest festival celebrating the sun transition into Capricorn. Festive cooking incorporates freshly harvested herbs and leaves.
festivals.description_hi: सूर्य के मकर राशि में प्रवेश का पावन सूर्योत्सव एवं फसलों का त्योहार।

checklist.purpose: Entrance decor and festive mango-leaf torans
checklist.notes: Symbolizes prosperity.

festivals.description_en: Celebration of sibling bonds and Vedic Upakarma ritual using sacred Durva and Tulsi for sanctification.
festivals.description_hi: भाई-बहन के स्नेह और रक्षा का पर्व तथा पवित्र यज्ञोपवीत उपाकर्म पूजन।

checklist.purpose: Auspicious grass placed in the Rakhi thali and Akshata
checklist.notes: Sign of purity and longevity.

checklist.purpose: Offering during morning puja rituals
checklist.notes: Spiritual sanctification.

festivals.description_en: Reverence to spiritual preceptors and commemoration of Buddha's enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.
festivals.description_hi: आध्यात्मिक गुरुओं के प्रति कृतज्ञता तथा बोधिवृक्ष के नीचे भगवान बुद्ध के ज्ञानोदय का स्मरण।

checklist.purpose: Meditation, circumambulation, and honor to the Bodhi lineage
checklist.notes: Find the nearest serene Peepal/Bodhi tree for quiet contemplation.

plants.address_hint: Near Assi Ghat entrance pathway, under stone pavilion
plants.notes: Mature Bael tree with abundant trifoliate leaves, revered by local morning bathers and pujaris.
plants.heritage_story: Planted over 60 years ago; devotees collect Belpatra for morning Vishwanath offerings.

plants.address_hint: Tulsi Ghat, adjacent to Akhada platform
plants.notes: Massive sacred Peepal overlooking the Ganga river steps. Excellent cooling shade.
plants.heritage_story: Associated with Goswami Tulsidas tradition along the Ghats.

plants.address_hint: BHU Campus, Botanical Garden outskirts near New Vishwanath Temple
plants.notes: Wild Dhatura shrubs bearing characteristic spiky round fruits and purple-white trumpet blossoms.

plants.address_hint: Sigra Stadium Road, public park corner
plants.notes: Young healthy Shami tree. Frequently visited during Dussehra for auspicious leaves.

plants.address_hint: Eco Park (Rajdhani Vatika), Section 2 walking trail
plants.notes: Ancient spreading Neem tree with dense medicinal foliage. Great air and cooling shade.

plants.address_hint: Gandhi Maidan perimeter lawn, near Gate 4
plants.notes: Lush green patches of 3-bladed Durva grass. Regularly clipped by park caretakers.

plants.address_hint: Boring Road, residential avenue garden boundary
plants.notes: Large Langra mango tree. Owner permits harvesting fresh leaves for festivals and Kalash pujas.

plants.address_hint: Behind Mahavir Mandir campus, Station Road
plants.notes: Sacred Bael tree in temple garden courtyard. Leaves harvested for Hanuman ji and Shiva worship.
plants.heritage_story: Supplies belpatra for thousands of devotees during Sawan and Shivratri.

plants.address_hint: Lodhi Gardens, near Sikandar Lodi Tomb
plants.notes: Majestic heritage Neem tree providing broad canopy. Tagged and maintained by NDMC.
plants.heritage_story: Over 80 years old, one of the heritage trees of the Lodhi historical precinct.

plants.address_hint: Sundar Nursery, Heritage section near water canal
plants.notes: Exemplary sprawling Banyan tree with numerous descending aerial roots. Popular landmark.
plants.heritage_story: Planted during the early 20th-century botanical landscaping of central Delhi.

plants.address_hint: Central Ridge Forest edge, near talkatora garden gate
plants.notes: Parijat tree blooming with fragrant orange-stemmed white flowers in early dawn.

plants.address_hint: Protected botanical research grove (Area centroid shown)
plants.notes: Protected specimen. Coordinates fuzzed for conservation security.

plants.address_hint: Cubbon Park, near Band Stand lawn
plants.notes: Sprawling mature Banyan tree. Shade point for walkers and weekend book clubs.
plants.heritage_story: Witness to Bengaluru's transformation, over 120 years old.

plants.address_hint: Basavanagudi, residential street green verge near DVG Road
plants.notes: Healthy aromatic Curry leaf tree. Neighbors harvest fresh sprigs for daily Rasam and Sambhar.

plants.address_hint: Lalbagh Botanical Garden, Medicinal Plants section
plants.notes: High yielding gooseberry tree. In fruit during late autumn.

plants.address_hint: Botanical Conservatory Grove (Area centroid displayed for safety)
plants.notes: Protected endangered endemic timber species. Exact location obscured to prevent poaching.
